name: Ishmaelites
summary: The twelve tribes descended from Ishmael, Abraham's first son by Hagar the Egyptian, who lived as desert nomads and caravan traders across northern Arabia. It was an Ishmaelite caravan, loaded with spices for Egypt, that bought Joseph. Arab tradition has long counted Ishmael as a forefather of the northern Arabs.
name_meaning: Ishmael: 'God hears' — named by the angel because 'the LORD hath heard thy affliction'.

origin.account: When Sarai was barren she gave her Egyptian maid Hagar to Abram, and Hagar bore Ishmael. After Isaac's birth Hagar and Ishmael were sent away. In the wilderness of Beer-sheba God heard the lad's voice and promised, 'I will make him a great nation.' Ishmael grew up in the wilderness of Paran, became an archer, and married an Egyptian wife.

lineage.ancestor: Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar
lineage.notes: God promised that Ishmael would father 'twelve princes'. They were Nebajoth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish and Kedemah. Esau married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath. Jetur and Naphish appear later as the Hagarites east of Gilead, whom the Transjordan tribes defeated.

homeland.region: From Havilah to Shur — the deserts of northern Arabia and Sinai
homeland.description: Ishmael's sons 'dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that is before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria' — the great arc of desert from the edge of Egypt across northern Arabia towards Mesopotamia. Their tribes controlled oasis towns and the incense-and-spice caravan routes.
homeland.modern_location: Northern Saudi Arabia, Jordan's eastern desert, southern Syria and Iraq's western desert, and Sinai.

places.name: Beer-lahai-roi
places.note: The well where the angel met Hagar: 'Thou God seest me'.

places.name: Tema
places.note: Oasis named after Ishmael's son; the Babylonian king Nabonidus lived there for ten years.

places.name: Dumah
places.note: Oasis named after Ishmael's son; seat of Qedarite queens in Assyrian records.

places.name: Kedar
places.note: The most powerful Ishmaelite tribe: 'the tents of Kedar'.

timeline.event: Ishmael born; God promises to multiply him.
Ishmael, aged thirteen, is circumcised with Abraham — the first to receive the covenant sign alongside him.
Hagar and Ishmael are sent away; God provides a well.
Isaac and Ishmael bury Abraham together at Machpelah. Ishmael dies aged 137.
Ishmaelite traders from Gilead, carrying spicery, balm and myrrh, buy Joseph for twenty pieces of silver.
Obil the Ishmaelite keeps David's camels.
Assyrian kings fight and tax the Qedarite Arabs and their queens (Zabibe, Samsi); the prophets pronounce 'the burden upon Arabia'.
Paul uses Hagar and Sarah as an allegory of two covenants — bondage and freedom.

gods: Pre-Islamic Arabian deities (e.g. Allat/Atarsamain in Qedarite records)
religion.practices: Ishmael himself was circumcised into Abraham's covenant and blessed by God. His descendants later worshipped Arabian gods; Assyrian kings took Qedarite idols as trophies and sometimes returned them.

importance: Ishmael's story shows God's care for those on the edges of the covenant family. The first person in Scripture to give God a name was Hagar, an Egyptian slave: 'Thou God seest me.' Ishmael's very name means 'God hears'. The chosen line ran through Isaac, yet God blessed Ishmael too and kept his promise to make him a great nation. The Ishmaelite caravan that bought Joseph was the unwitting means by which God preserved Israel in the famine.

impact.how: Met by God twice in the wilderness and given promises for her son.
Carried to Egypt by Ishmaelite traders.
Married Mahalath, Ishmael's daughter, to please his father.
Hagar and Ishmael became Paul's picture of life under the law versus the promise.

notable_people.name: Ishmael
notable_people.role: Son of Abraham, father of twelve princes

notable_people.name: Nebajoth and Kedar
notable_people.role: Ishmael's eldest sons; Isaiah foresees their flocks at God's altar

notable_people.name: Geshem the Arabian
notable_people.role: Opposed Nehemiah (an Arab chief of Qedar, per the Tell el-Maskhuta bowl)

key_verses.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto her, Behold, thou art with child, and shalt bear a son, and shalt call his name Ishmael; because the LORD hath heard thy affliction.
And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation.

And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is.  Arise, lift up the lad, and hold him in thine hand; for I will make him a great nation.

And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.

fate.summary: The Ishmaelite tribes did not disappear. Kedar, Nebaioth, Dumah and Tema are recorded in Assyrian and Babylonian texts as Arab tribes and oases through the 7th–5th centuries BC. They merged into the wider Arab peoples of the peninsula.

today.summary: Arab and Islamic tradition regards Ishmael (Isma'il) as the ancestor of the northern Arabs ('Adnanites), and traces the Prophet Muhammad's lineage to him. The Bible does not make that specific link. Modern historians treat these genealogies as traditional rather than documented. The oases named after Ishmael's sons — Tayma, Dumat al-Jandal — are still inhabited in Saudi Arabia.
today.descendants: Traditionally, many Arab tribes of northern and central Arabia.
today.modern_legacy: Ishmael and Hagar hold an honoured place in Islam. Muslim tradition connects Hagar's search for water to the rite of sa'i at Mecca.

archaeology.name: Assyrian annals of Tiglath-pileser III, Sennacherib, Esarhaddon and Ashurbanipal
archaeology.significance: Record wars with Qedar (Qidri), Nebaioth (Nabayati), Dumah (Adummatu) and Arab queens.

archaeology.name: Tell el-Maskhuta silver bowl
archaeology.significance: Dedicated by 'Qainu son of Gashmu, king of Qedar' — likely the son of Nehemiah's opponent Geshem the Arabian.

archaeology.name: Tayma inscriptions
archaeology.significance: Record the Babylonian king Nabonidus' long stay at Tema.
